entities.evidence: Methuselah, the son of Enoch named in Genesis 5:21, fathers Lamech at age 187.
This verse names Methuselah as Lamech’s father. The Lamech in Genesis 4:18 is the son of Methushael.

analysis.evidence: Methuselah is the subject of וַיְחִי. The following number phrase gives the 187 years he lived before he fathered Lamech.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־. The verb has the shortened form יְחִי.
analysis.sense: live for a stated length of time

analysis.evidence: מְתוּשֶׁלַח is the subject of וַיְחִי and remains the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד אֶת לָמֶךְ. The verse says that Methuselah fathered Lamech at age 187.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: שֶׁבַע וּשְׁמֹנִים שָׁנָה means “seven and eighty years.” שֶׁבַע supplies the units in Methuselah’s age of 187 years at Lamech’s birth.
שֶׁבַע וּשְׁמֹנִים שָׁנָה means ‘seven and eighty years.’ The marked numeral supplies the eighty in Methuselah’s age of 187 years, with וּמְאַת שָׁנָה adding the hundred.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ plus cardinal numeral, common gender, plural absolute.

analysis.evidence: In שֶׁבַע וּשְׁמֹנִים שָׁנָה, the marked noun supplies the unit for eighty-seven. וּמְאַת שָׁנָה adds a hundred years, giving Methuselah’s age as 187 when he fathered Lamech.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: וּמְאַת שָׁנָה adds a hundred years to the preceding eighty-seven, giving Methuselah’s age as 187 when he fathered Lamech.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ prefixed to the singular construct numeral מְאַת.

analysis.evidence: In וּמְאַת שָׁנָה, “and a hundred years,” שָׁנָה supplies the unit counted by מְאַת. This hundred adds to the preceding eighty-seven years, giving Methuselah’s age of 187 when he fathered Lamech.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Methuselah is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד, and אֶת marks Lamech as its direct object. After giving Methuselah’s age, the verse records that he fathered Lamech.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix

analysis.evidence: In וַיּוֹלֶד אֶת לָמֶךְ, Methuselah fathered Lamech. אֶת marks the personal name לָמֶךְ as the definite direct object of וַיּוֹלֶד.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle, without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for לֶמֶךְ with the derivation left open.
draft.definition: A Hebrew masculine personal name, borne here by the son of Methuselah.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:25 names the child in וַיּוֹלֶד אֶת לָמֶךְ, “and he fathered Lamech.”

analysis.evidence: Methuselah is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד, “he fathered.” The direct-object marker אֶת introduces לָמֶךְ as the name of his child. The verse gives no derivation for the name.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name in the verse-final pausal form לָמֶךְ, with no prefix or suffix.
